A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CB-pLM research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original perplexity measurements, protein concept-control experiments, Siltuximab redesigns, attribution comparisons, and appendix experiments on species steering and Color-MNIST.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and additionally reports Mason antibody perplexities, masking-rate sensitivity, additional Siltuximab baselines, and structure-based assessments.

M1.justification: Appendix A.1 revises the stated orthogonality objective from comparisons between w_i and w_{k+1}, averaged over k concepts, to comparisons between z and unknown token embeddings, averaged over sequence positions. This is a localized revision to the written loss; the architecture and intervention algorithm remain unchanged, and implementation changes or retraining are not established.

E1.justification: Section 3.1 replaces the unnamed held-out perplexity benchmark with the Mason antibody dataset. UniRef50/SWISS-PROT training, the 14-concept control tasks, Siltuximab, species steering, and Color-MNIST remain. The coverage change is concentrated in the model-quality evaluation.

E2.justification: The Siltuximab comparison adds ESM2 and Hydrophilic Resample alongside WJS, PropEn, and LaMBO-2, with participation verified in Figure 7. ESM2 already appeared in v1's perplexity comparison, but its Siltuximab participation is new. The principal conditional-model and attribution comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 specifies 10,000 randomly sampled Mason antibodies and adds 650M/3B ESM2 configurations to the perplexity evaluation. Appendix C.1.1 adds a 25% masking test alongside the retained 5% tests. Appendix C.2.2 introduces predicted-structure TAP metrics and a 5% proximity acceptance filter, substantially extending evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: New Figures 17–19 test whether the control advantage persists at 25% masking. New Figures 22–23 examine whether Siltuximab redesigns preserve structural surface properties and pass a proximity filter. These add sensitivity and independent property-preservation analyses beyond v1's likelihood-based naturalness assessment; earlier attribution, correlation, and debugging analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The added distributions and acceptance percentages do not introduce a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: The perplexity results are replaced: CB-pLM's 24M/150M values change from 11.57/10.49 on the held-out benchmark to 4.29/3.20 on Mason, which is not a same-setting improvement. New Figure 17 reports 25%-masking accuracy of 98.9% for CB-pLM versus 73.6%/81.6% for C-pLM/CC-pLM. Additional Siltuximab baseline results and TAP distributions/filter outcomes materially expand the reported evidence.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1, Equation (1), changes the quantities and averaging domain in the formal orthogonality-loss definition, rather than merely renaming symbols. No new theorem or proof is added; the attribution formulas and their Taylor-approximation explanation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: controllable, interpretable, debuggable protein language models, approximately threefold stronger concept changes, and scaling from 24M to 3B parameters with comparable perplexity. The new experiments support existing contributions.

C2.justification: Section 6 now explicitly leaves unseen-concept generalization on proteins to future work, distinguishing it from the retained toy demonstration. Section 3.1 adds the interpretation that learning biophysical concepts might improve model quality. The new TAP discussion interprets structural-property preservation as additional evidence of naturalness; existing concept-leakage limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds ESM2's 150M configuration, UniRef50 pretraining and logit sampling, the Hydrophilic Resample residue set, and the ABodyBuilder2/TAP assessment workflow and filtering threshold. Existing training configurations and the code/model repository access statement are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for Mason, ImmuneBuilder/ABodyBuilder2, TAP, and hydrophilic residue selection, and removes Perez et al.'s red-teaming citation with the rewritten debugging introduction. The broader positioning relative to concept bottleneck models, conditional protein models, and sparse autoencoders is retained.

P1.justification: Sections 3.1, 5.2, and the discussion receive localized rewrites; Section 5.1 adds a local/global interpretability explanation. v2 also adds acknowledgements and subdivides Appendix C.2. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact, and the new-concept extension discussion remains in Appendix E.2 despite its removal from the main discussion.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains tag/conditioning indicators and additional model-size columns, and Figure 7 is redrawn for the expanded comparator set. Five new appendix figures display masking sensitivity and TAP assessments. Several retained plots are resized or relocated, producing a substantial expansion and rearrangement of the empirical displays while preserving the general document style.

improvement.justification: The added Siltuximab controls, masking sensitivity test, and predicted-structure TAP checks strengthen evidence beyond v1's likelihood-based naturalness assessment. Explicitly identifying unseen-concept generalization on proteins as untested also improves qualification. These are useful, focused gains: the original held-out perplexity results are replaced rather than retained alongside Mason, and Section 3.1's 'higher perplexity' wording remains inconsistent with most Table 1 comparisons.
